verdict.rationale: Cognee documents a full conversational memory loop. `remember()` writes content into permanent graph memory or a session cache tied to a session_id. `improve()` is used at the end of a chat or agent session to bridge short-term session memory into permanent memory. `recall()` is the main retrieval entry point and automatically picks a retrieval strategy. Founder posts say the engine combines graph and vector stores. missing for 10: first-party docs explicitly describing semantic/vector similarity search in recall, independent or hands-on corroboration of cross-session recall quality.

support.subject: As a developer, I can add memories from conversations and retrieve them later with semantic search, so context persists across sessions

citations.quote: The `.remember` operation is the main ingestion entry point in Cognee v1.0. It stores information in memory with a single API call.
cognee.remember(data, session_id="my_session") — writes content directly into the session cache for fast retrieval.
Use it at the end of a chat or agent session to bridge short-term session memory into permanent memory.
The `.recall` operation is the main retrieval entry point in Cognee v1.0. It searches memory using the best available source for the request.
Store data as permanent graph memory or fast session memory in one call.
